questions.answer: I do, casually at least. I mostly take photos on my phone when I travel or see something striking. I'm no expert, but I love the idea of [[preserving]] a moment so I can look back on it later.

questions.q: What do you usually take photos of?
questions.answer: Mostly landscapes and family moments. The Jamuna at sunset is a favourite subject, because the light on the water is just [[breathtaking]]. I also take lots of pictures of my nephew whenever we visit my sister in Dhaka.

questions.q: Do you like keeping photos of special events?
questions.answer: Definitely. I love looking back at photos from trips and celebrations, because they bring the feelings of that day rushing back. They're some of my most [[treasured]] possessions, honestly.

questions.q: Do you prefer printed photos or keeping them on your phone?
questions.answer: Practically, I keep almost everything on my phone, but I have a real soft spot for printed photos. My mother still has old albums from her wedding, and flicking through them together has a [[nostalgic]] charm that scrolling never quite matches.

questions.q: Do you think people take too many photos nowadays?
questions.answer: I think so, yes. Because it costs nothing, people snap hundreds of pictures and hardly ever look at them again. Sometimes I feel we're so busy [[capturing]] a moment that we forget to actually enjoy it.
